items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he listened to Schoenberg, “Pierrot Lunaire,” yeah, when I was a kid.

ctx.x: You have a story I read about Charlie Parker, where you discovered that he listened to Charles Ives.

No, he listened to Schoenberg, “Pierrot Lunaire,” yeah, when I was a kid. I mean, with Bird’s and he listened to Bartok, he liked Bartkok and Schoenberg. So, I remember going to the library and getting um uh … Stravinsky was not quite so deep and Bartok was sort of in the pocket. But I think when my parents heard me listening “Pierrot Lunaire,” you know, the early 12 tone stuff, which is really “out” [makes weird noises to demonstrate], you know, [laughs] wild intervals. I think my parents were quite ready to…
Is there anything that you’re listening to right now that perhaps fans could say, “Hey I want to go check that out because Phil Woods is checking it out.“ [END TRACK 3 DISC 2 BEGIN TRACK 1 DISC 3]
